seo.h1: M-886 Titanium Dioxide for Plastics and Masterbatch Evaluation

hero.summaryLead: A chloride-process rutile titanium dioxide pigment documented for polyolefin masterbatch, high-temperature extrusion and cast-film processing, and engineering plastics.
hero.summaryBody: The current M-886 product profile identifies excellent dispersion, a bright white color and good processing with minimal effect on melt flow as evaluation directions. Review the typical product data below and confirm suitability through testing in your own polymer system, formulation, processing and end-use conditions.

positioning.heading: Where M-886 Fits in Product Evaluation
positioning.lead: M-886 is a rutile titanium dioxide pigment for plastics produced by the chloride process.
positioning.body: Its documented public profile covers polyolefin masterbatch, high-temperature extrusion and cast-film processing, and engineering plastics. Use M-886 as an evaluation candidate when dispersion, bright-white color direction and processing behavior are relevant. Final Grade selection should account for the polymer, carrier resin, additive package, pigment loading, processing temperature, equipment, end-use requirements and destination-document needs.
decisionPoints: High-temperature extrusion and cast-film processing direction
Evaluation of dispersion, bright-white color and melt-flow behavior

applications.heading: Plastics and Masterbatch Directions to Evaluate
applications.intro: Review each documented direction in your own polymer system, processing and end-use conditions.

items.title: Polyolefin Masterbatches
items.body: Evaluate M-886 at the intended pigment loading and carrier-resin system. Confirm dispersion, color direction, processing behavior and downstream dilution performance under the actual masterbatch conditions.

items.title: High-Temperature Extrusion and Cast-Film Processing
items.body: Review M-886 under the intended high-temperature extrusion and cast-film conditions. Confirm dispersion, color, film appearance, processing stability and melt-flow behavior in the complete polymer formulation.

items.title: Engineering Plastics
items.body: Include M-886 in engineering-plastics testing using the actual polymer, additives, pigment loading, processing temperature and equipment. Confirm appearance, dispersion, processing behavior and end-use suitability.

evaluation.heading: What to Evaluate in Your Plastics Formulation
evaluation.intro: Use the documented M-886 profile and typical data to frame buyer testing.

groups.heading: Dispersion and Appearance Review
items: Dispersion behavior at the intended pigment loading and mixing conditions
Bright-white color direction in the complete formulation
Finished appearance in the selected polymer system
Color and dispersion consistency after downstream processing

groups.heading: Processing and Qualification Review
items: Melt-flow behavior under the intended formulation and processing conditions
High-temperature extrusion or cast-film conditions, where applicable
Compatibility with the selected resin, carrier and additive package
End-use requirements, destination-document needs and sample-validation results

evaluation.disclaimer: These evaluation priorities identify what to check during buyer testing. They do not guarantee a fixed result in every polymer, process or end-use environment.
